chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Qulawayh from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdallah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:

We were at Abu Abdillah's (peace be upon him) place when he said: Do you not have a secure shelter? Do you not have a comforter whom you can seek comfort in? What prevents you from [referring to] al-Harith bin al-Mughira al-Nasri?

key_terms.الْحَارِثُ بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ النَّصْرِيُ: Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, a companion known for truthfulness
key_terms.مُسْتَرَاح: A source of comfort or rest
key_terms.مُفْزَع: A place of refuge or security

ai.seo_question: Who is al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri and why did the Imam recommend him?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri as a primary 'refuge' (muf'azz) for his companions, a term in Shia hadith criticism denoting a trustworthy narrator whose solitary report (khabar al-wahid) is accepted as authoritative proof. This narration underscores the practical reliance on specific, verified scholars during the Minor Occultation to preserve religious knowledge and resolve jurisprudential matters without requiring consensus.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/-] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Qulawayh from Sa’d b. Abdallah from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from Abdallah b. Muhammad al-Hajjal from Yunus b. Ya’qub who said:

we were at Aba Abdillah’s عليه السلام place when he said: do you not have a secure shelter? do you not have a comforter whom you can seek comfort in? what prevents you from [referring to] al-Harith bin al-Mughira al-Nasri.
